answer: A bonded reputation ledger resists fake identities: each agent must stake value and build a verifiable history before it can transact at scale. Like a lotus that only opens after steady growth, trust is earned slowly, not claimed instantly. A raven-like audit trail links actions to one identity, so splitting into many copies dilutes reputation instead of multiplying it. When a flood tide of new fake accounts appears, rate limits and rising stake requirements make each extra identity costly, so creating thousands costs far more than any fraud could gain.
